outcome: Help care-management teams identify cohorts for preventive outreach with explainable evidence and equitable human review.
overview: Preventive needs surface across fragmented claims, clinical and social data — often only after avoidable deterioration has begun. This solution assembles governed data into explainable risk and eligibility views that help care-management teams identify cohorts for preventive outreach: risk contributors are visible, prohibited features are excluded, and fairness is monitored across subgroups. Care managers review every cohort before any outreach, consent and capacity rules are enforced, and outcomes and equity are tracked on a shared dashboard. A 10–16-week retrospective validation precedes operational use, targeting more precise cohort identification, more completed preventive outreach and measurable, fairly distributed utilisation change over six to twelve months.

benefits.text: Identify approved outreach cohorts faster and more precisely than manual registry review
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Precision is validated retrospectively against the customer’s own labels before any operational use; clinician-in-the-loop review of every cohort is mandatory

benefits.text: Increase completed preventive outreach within existing care-management capacity
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on the customer’s intervention capacity — the solution queues within stated capacity rather than expanding it

benefits.text: Monitor fairness across agreed subgroups on every model and queue
benefits.source: Reference architecture fairness-monitoring design, Redington Healthcare catalogue,
benefits.limits: Monitoring is a design property; meeting fairness thresholds is validated per model and population, not assumed

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); clinical and claims data stay in the customer tenancy in the reference designs, in line with UAE and Saudi health-data regulations

notFor.situation: No intervention capacity or outreach programme to act on identified cohorts
notFor.why: Risk identification without an intervention pathway creates surveillance, not prevention — the catalogue requires intervention capacity as a profile precondition

notFor.situation: No outcome data or labels to validate against
notFor.why: Model validation and the benefit case both depend on historical outcomes; without them precision claims cannot be tested

notFor.situation: Expectation of causal savings claims without a comparison design
notFor.why: Attributable utilisation change requires a valid evaluation design; the source catalogue explicitly rules out causal claims without one

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns clinical review, consent policy, equity thresholds and the evaluation design · Duration: 10–16-week validation; 20–32 weeks to operational deployment
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, data engineer, data scientist; customer population-health lead, medical director, care-management lead, actuary, privacy and equity owners · Support model: Business-hours or 24×7 option; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Intervention, data and consent discovery
2) Data integration and feature-layer build
3) Retrospective validation with subgroup analysis
4) Care-manager co-design and queue calibration
5) Operational pilot with the agreed evaluation design
6) Stabilisation, outcome review and handover
deliverables: Clinical-utility thresholds met in retrospective validation
Fairness thresholds met across agreed subgroups
Queue volumes respect stated care-management capacity
Consent and privacy controls verified; case-system integration reconciled
A valid comparison design in place for outcome attribution
